question: If a car travelling along a straight road increases its speed by unequal amounts in equal intervals of time, then the car is said to be moving with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**non-uniform acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration:**
 
• Non-uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity of an object changes by unequal amounts in equal intervals of time.
 
• This means the rate of change of velocity is not constant.
 
• In simpler terms, the car is speeding up or slowing down at a changing rate.
 
• This is common in real-world scenarios, such as driving in traffic or on a winding road.
 
• The acceleration can be increasing, decreasing, or even changing direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform velocity:**
 
• Uniform velocity implies that an object is moving at a constant speed in a straight line.
 
• This means there is no change in either the speed or the direction of motion.
 
• If the speed increases by unequal amounts, the velocity is not uniform.
 
• Uniform velocity would mean zero acceleration.
 
• This is rarely found in real world driving situations.
 
• **Uniform speed:**
 
• Uniform speed means that an object is moving at a constant speed, but it does not specify the direction.
 
• While the speed is constant, the direction could change, resulting in acceleration.
 
• If the speed is increasing by unequal amounts, the speed is not uniform.
 
• Uniform speed does not mean uniform velocity.
 
• Uniform speed means the magnitude of the velocity is constant.
 
• **Uniform acceleration:**
 
• Uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity of an object changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time.
 
• This means the rate of change of velocity is constant.
 
• In simpler terms, the car is speeding up or slowing down at a constant rate.
 
• An example of this is a freely falling object.
 
• This situation is not what is described in the provided question.
